docs.title: Removed settings
docs.text:
These WingFlight settings went with the aircraft features (angle and leveling, acro trainer, attitude hold, GPS rescue and navigation, thrust vectoring, the governor, cross-axis, snap and prop-hang relax):

  • governor_*, gps_rescue_*, nav_*, tv_*, angle_*, acro_trainer_*, atthold_*, cross_axis_relax_*, snap_relax_*, prop_hang_* and failsafe_stick_threshold
  • the tv_profile command

Pasting a diff from WingFlight or older Gripora reports these lines as unknown; they can be ignored. Settings whose range or defaults changed for a car (for example model_type, map, fw_spa_speed_max, the throttle and failsafe defaults) were reset to the new defaults when the firmware was upgraded, so check them after restoring an old backup.

docs.title: Debug modes
docs.text:
debug_mode picks what the Blackbox debug fields record. Gripora's own modes:

DRIVE shows the drive state:

Field Value 0 Throttle command, x1000 1 Commanded ESC state: 0 neutral, 1 forward, 2 brake, 3 reverse 2 Travel direction (+1 forward, -1 reverse) 3 Speed, 0.1 km/h 4 Speed known (1 = there is an RPM source) 5 Gyro correction scale, x1000 6 Motor 1 RPM 7 Stopped (1 = RPM shows the car stopped)

DRIVE_AIDS shows the drive aids:

Field Value 0 Throttle from the transmitter, x1000 (below 0 is brake/reverse) 1 Throttle to the ESC, x1000 2 Flags: bit 0 aids on, bit 1 ABS armed, bit 2 ABS releasing, bit 3 traction control armed, bit 4 traction control holding the throttle back, bit 5 launch staged, bit 6 launching 3 While braking with ABS: pulse rate, x10 Hz. While driving forward with traction control or launching: the throttle allowed, x1000 4 ABS release brake (floor), x1000 5 ABS hold, ms 6 Time into the current ABS pulse, ms 7 Steering, x1000

GAIN_ATTEN shows the throttle (TPA) and speed (SPA) gain attenuation that scales P, D, F and B:

Field Value 0 Throttle attenuation, x1000 (1000 = 100%) 1 Speed attenuation, x1000 2 Speed used by the curve, 0.1 km/h (motor RPM wheel speed, else GPS) 3 Raw GPS speed, cm/s 4 GPS fix (1 = fix)

ALTITUDE shows the altitude estimate next to its sources:

Field Value 0 Altitude, cm (what telemetry uses) 1 Vario, cm/s 2 Measured altitude before fusion, cm 3 Measured vario (derivative of the measured altitude), cm/s 4 Barometer altitude, cm 5 GPS altitude, cm 6 Vertical acceleration, gravity removed, cm/s² 7 Learned accelerometer error, cm/s²

Altitude comes from the accelerometer fused with a measured altitude: the barometer, or GPS altitude on boards without one (position_* settings above).

Modes that no longer record anything are named UNUSED_<n>, where <n> is the mode's number. The numbers are unchanged, so older logs still decode, but a diff that sets one of the old names is rejected as an invalid value. Set debug_mode = NONE instead.

Number Old name 8 RC_SETPOINT 25-27 RANGEFINDER, RANGEFINDER_QUALITY, LIDAR_TF 29 GOVERNOR 30 SDIO 33 SMARTAUDIO 34 RTH 36 ACRO_TRAINER 46-47 TTA, AIRBORNE 54 GPS_RESCUE_THROTTLE_PID 56-57 FEEDFORWARD_LIMIT, FEEDFORWARD 61-62 D_LPF, VTX_TRAMP 69-77 PITCH_PRECOMP, YAW_PRECOMP, RESCUE, RESCUE_ALTHOLD, CROSS_COUPLING, ERROR_DECAY, HS_OFFSET, HS_BLEED, GOV_MOTOR 79-81 AUTOHOVER, ATTHOLD, TVHOLD 83-84 SNAP_RELAX, PROP_HANG

docs.title: Servos
docs.text:
There are 24 servos. Servo N is sent on PWM output N, where the board has one, and on bus channel N (see fbus_master_channels and sbus_out_channels above, and the Servos tab; channels past the count are sent at centre). The servo command lists the servos in use and sets one:

servo <index> <mid> <min> <max> <rneg> <rpos> <speed> <flags>
Argument Range Default Meaning <index> 1 to 24 The servo <mid> 1000 to 2000 1500 Center, µs <min> -1000 to 0 -600 Lower travel limit, µs from center <max> 0 to 1000 600 Upper travel limit, µs from center <rneg>, <rpos> 50 to 1000 500 Scale on the negative and positive side, µs <speed> 0 to 60000 0 Speed limit, ms per 60°; 0 is no limit <flags> 0 Bit 0 reverse, bit 1 geometry correction

The signal sent to a servo stays within 880-2159 µs. servo status, servo override, servo trim and servo name use the same index.

servo name lists the servos that have a name, servo name <index> <name> sets one and servo name <index> clears it. A name is up to 8 printable characters and may contain spaces:

servo name 1 STEER
servo name 2 REAR STR

Names are labels only; nothing reads them while driving. diff and dump include them.

Backups from before MSP API 22.16

The servo line had a ninth value, a rate per servo, between <rpos> and <speed>. Such a line is still accepted and its rate is ignored. bus_servo_clone_pwm no longer exists. A servo, servo trim or mixer rule line that names servo 9 or above meant a bus channel 8 lower than it does now, so don't paste those lines back as they are.

docs.title: Mixer rules
docs.text:
mixer rule <index> <operator> <input> <output> <weight> <offset> <weight-neg> <speed> <curve> <condition> <role>

Everything after <offset> is optional: <weight-neg> defaults to the symmetric value, and the rest default to off. <operator> is set, add or mul; mixer rule <index> del deletes a rule and mixer rule reset goes back to the default rules. dump and diff print rules in this form, with names for the input and output. The default rules are the car preset (see Car Mixer, Channels and Gyro Direction):

mixer rule 0 set SY S1 1000 0 1000 0 0 0 0
mixer rule 1 set ST M1 1000 0 1000 0 0 0 0

Stabilized steering (SY) drives servo 1 and stabilized throttle (ST) drives motor 1. The drive aids work on the stabilized throttle, so an ESC rule fed from the RC throttle (CT or RT) bypasses them.

<output> is a number or a name:

Output Name Meaning 0 - None 1-24 S1-S24 Servos 1-24 25-26 R25, R26 Reserved 27-30 M1-M4 Motors 1-4

<input> is a number or a name:

Input Name Meaning 0 None 1-4 SR, SP, SY, ST Stabilized roll, pitch, steering, throttle. Roll and pitch are always zero 5-8 CR, CP, CY, CT RC command (stick deflection after the deadband) roll, pitch, steering, throttle 9-12 RR, RP, RY, RT RC channel roll, pitch, steering, throttle 13-26 AUX1-AUX3, CH8-CH18 RC channels 5-18 27-29 TR, TP, TY Reserved (thrust vectoring removed), always zero 30-35 CH19-CH24 RC channels 19-24

RC channels here are in the firmware's own order (roll, pitch, steering, throttle, then AUX), after the map command has been applied, not the order on the receiver. With the default car map RT1234AE, CH1 is steering, CH2 throttle, CH3-CH6 AUX1-AUX4 and CH7/CH8 roll and pitch.

The optional last argument, <role>, is a label for the Configurator: 0 none (the default when omitted), 1 Flap Compensation, 2 Differential Thrust Yaw. Both named roles are inherited from WingFlight aircraft mixes; the mixer never reads the role, and the Configurator only offers none. See Mixer.

docs.title: FBUS/S.Port Sensor ID Reference
docs.text: Background reference for the FBUS/S.Port Sensors tab -- what the Physical ID and App ID numbers it shows actually mean. These IDs come from FrSky's S.Port sensor addressing scheme, which FBUS reuses; they're shared across the wider FrSky/OpenTX/EdgeTX ecosystem, not specific to Gripora.

docs.title: Physical IDs
docs.text:
A sensor's Physical ID identifies what kind of sensor it is -- fixed by the sensor's own firmware/hardware, not something you configure. Multiple sensors of different types can share a bus; each announces itself with its own Physical ID.

ID (hex) ID (dec) Name Notes 0x00 0 VARIO2 Variometer (altitude/climb rate) 0x01 1 FLVSS Per-cell LiPo voltage sensor 0x02 2 CURRENT Current/voltage sensor 0x03 3 GPS Position, altitude, speed, course, time, satellite count 0x04 4 RPM RPM sensor (also reports temperature) 0x05 5 SP2UART_A S.Port-to-UART bridge (host side) 0x06 6 SP2UART_B S.Port-to-UART bridge (remote side) 0x07 7 FAS_150S High-current sensor 0x08 8 SBEC Smart BEC voltage/current sensor 0x09 9 AIR_SPEED Airspeed (pitot) sensor 0x0A 10 ESC ESC telemetry (voltage, current, RPM, temperature, consumption) 0x0B 11 PSD_30 Power sensor 0x0C 12 XACT_SERVO Smart bus-servo telemetry (current, voltage, temperature) 0x10 16 SD1 SD card logger module 0x12 18 VS600 FrSky VS600 module 0x16 22 GASSUIT Gas engine sensor suite (RPM, temperature, fuel) 0x17 23 FSD FrSky FSD module 0x18 24 GATEWAY FrSky Gateway 0x19 25 REDUNDANCY_BUS Redundancy-receiver bus sensor 0x1A 26 S6R FrSky S6R stabilization receiver telemetry

An unrecognized Physical ID shows up in the sensor table as ID_<n> rather than a name -- the sensor is still read and can still be forwarded, Gripora just doesn't have a friendly name for it.

docs.title: App IDs
docs.text:
Within a single sensor's data stream, App IDs identify the specific data type of each value it reports -- e.g. a GPS sensor reports latitude, altitude, speed, course, and time as separate App IDs, all under the same Physical ID. Related values are typically grouped in a contiguous 16-value range (BASE to BASE + 0x0F); the low nibble often carries a per-frame sequence bit and isn't meaningful on its own.

Base (hex) Base (dec) Sensor Data 0x0200 512 CURRENT Current, 0.1A steps 0x0210 528 CURRENT Voltage, 0.01V steps 0x0220 544 CURRENT Current, 0.001A steps (high precision) 0x0300 768 FLVSS Packed per-cell voltages, 0.002V steps 0x0400 1024 RPM Temperature 1 0x0410 1040 RPM Temperature 2 0x0500 1280 RPM RPM value 0x0800 2048 GPS Latitude/longitude (bit 31 selects which) 0x0820 2080 GPS Altitude 0x0830 2096 GPS Ground speed 0x0840 2112 GPS Course 0x0850 2128 GPS UTC date/time 0x0860 2144 GPS Satellite count 0x0B50 2896 ESC Voltage/current 0x0B60 2912 ESC RPM/consumption 0x0B70 2928 ESC Temperature 0x6800 26624 XACT_SERVO Current/voltage/temperature

For example, a GPS sensor's App IDs column showing 2048, 2080, 2096, 2128 is lat/long, altitude, speed, and time -- not course or satellite count, which that particular GPS unit isn't reporting.

When an FBUS GPS does not report the satellite-count App ID (0x0860), Gripora shows the satellite count as 0 rather than guessing, so checks that need a minimum number of satellites (such as position_gps_min_sats for GPS altitude) are not satisfied by an unknown value.

If you want to use an older FBUS GPS that doesn't report a satellite count, set gps_fbus_assumed_sats in CLI. A value of 0 keeps the safe default above; a value from 1 to 50 is used only when the FBUS GPS has position data but does not report 0x0860. Real satellite count data always overrides the assumed value when the sensor provides it.

docs.title: Basics
docs.text:
'SPI RX' in Gripora is a framework that allows for radio chips to be connected directly to the controller's MCU, and to be controlled by the firmware. This allows for the implementation of the functionality that controls the radio chip, and translates the received signals into RC control signals as part of the firmware.

This has a number of advantages: - the RX can be directly added to the controller board, allowing for smaller builds (after all, not many people want to use a controller without an RX); - it does not require one or more extra UARTs on the controller, and there is no risk of problems caused by a wrong UART configuration; - it does not require an extra MCU to control the radio chip, and can therefore be produced / sold cheaper; - since the RX 'firmware' is part of the controller firmware, fixes and updates will be applied as part of controller firmware updates, eliminating the need for (often cumbersome) RX firmware updates.

But there are also disadvantages: - a controller board will only have one radio chip, and will only be able to support the RC protocols that are using this chip. Changing to a different protocol is often not possible.

docs.title: The FrSky SPI RX
docs.text:
This driver uses the SPI RX framework in Gripora to provide support for the FrSky 2.4 GHz RC protocols, based on a CC2500 radio chip, with additional support for a PA/LNA (power amplifier / low noise amplifier) chip with antenna diversity, in order to provide sufficient power / sensitivity for outdoor flying.

The supported protocols are:

docs.title: FrSky D
docs.text:
• 8 channels / 9 ms frame spacing;
  • called 'D8' in OpenTX;
  • integrated FrSky hub telemetry.

docs.title: FrSky X
docs.text:
• 8 channels / 9 ms frame spacing or 16 channels / 18 ms frame spacing;
  • called 'D16' in OpenTX;
  • integrated FrSky SmartPort telemetry (including support for MSP over Smartport / lua scripts in OpenTX);

docs.title: FrSky X LBT
docs.text:
• LBT protocol version compatible with EU;
  • 8 channels / 9 ms frame spacing or 16 channels / 18 ms frame spacing;
  • called 'D16' in OpenTX;
  • integrated FrSky SmartPort telemetry (including support for MSP over Smartport / lua scripts in OpenTX);

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. in Gripora Configurator, go to the 'Configuration' tab, in 'Receiver' box, select 'SPI RX support' for 'Receiver mode':
  1. in the 'SPI Bus Receiver Provider' drop down that appears, select 'FRSKY_D', 'FRSKY_X' or 'FRSKY_X_LBT' (depending on the desired protocol):
  1. click 'Save & Reboot'. After the reboot, the RX LED will confirm that the FrSky RX is active by blinking slowly;
  2. enter bind mode by either:
  3. pressing the 'Bind' button on the controller (if there is one and it's reachable);
  4. entering CLI, and typing 'bind_rx_spi[Enter]'.
  5. the controller will indicate that bind mode is active by changing the RX LED to be permanently on. Now, on your TX, enter bind mode for the selected FrSky protocol (see screenshots for OpenTX):

FrSky D protocol:

FrSky X and X_LBT protocol:

  1. Once binding has completed, the controller will indicate this by blinking the RX LED slowly. There's no indication on the CLI, but you can observe successful binding by quitting the bind mode on TX, and seeing if status doesn't list RXLOSS anymore in "Arming disable flags". A reboot of the controller is not required.

docs.title: Tips & Tricks
docs.text:
• the RX bind information is stored in the following CLI parameters: frsky_spi_tx_id (internal TX id), frsky_spi_offset (frequency offset), frsky_spi_bind_hop_data (frequency hop sequence), and frsky_x_rx_num (RX number; FrSky X only). These are printed as part of a CLI diff / dump, and will be restored after a firmware update, making it unnecessary to do another bind after the update;
  • resetting the above parameters to defaults will 'erase' the binding information;
  • the CLI parameter frsky_spi_autobind can be enabled to configure the FrSky SPI RX to attempt a bind on every power up. This is mostly useful for demonstration models that should bind to whatever TX is powered up in the vicinity.

docs.text:
